newsitem.title: USA: Accused N.J. teens' infant had brain defect - report.
newsitem.headline: Accused N.J. teens' infant had brain defect - report.

text.p: The newborn son of the New Jersey teenagers accused of his murder was diagnosed by the Delaware Medical Examiner's office as having abnormal clefts in his brain, according to a death certificate released on Monday.

While it was the first time the medical examiner has acknowledged the defect, called schizencephaly, the March 11 report repeats an earlier finding that Brian Peterson helped Amy Grossberg deliver a full term, live infant that died of "multiple skull fractures ... with ... haemorrhages, hypothermia and asphyxia."
The schizencephaly was described as "not related to cause of death."

Peterson's attorney Joseph Hurley said the significance of the condition depends on where the cleft was located in the brain. He declined further comment due to a gag order, but said that the new development was "interesting."
The baby's body was found in a plastic bag in a dumpster of the Newark, Delaware, motel where he was born on Nov. 12.
Medical Examiner Adrienne Sekula-Perlman said the injuries that caused death were "shaking and blunt force impact" and exposure to cold.

At a January court hearing, defence attorneys said their experts believed the infant would not have survived his own congenital deformities or the medical problems suffered by Grossberg early in her pregnancy.
Grossberg and Peterson have been charged with a capital crime and the state has said it will seek the death penalty.

In January, state prosecutors agreed to bail of $300,000 each for the former high school sweethearts' provided they be confined to their parents' Bergen County, New Jersey, homes and electronically monitored.
Before their arrest in November, Grossberg was a freshman art major at the University of Delaware in Newark, and Peterson was a freshman at Gettysburg College in Pennsylvania.
Their trial was set to begin on Sept. 9 in the Delaware Superior Court before Judge Henry DuPont Ridgely.
